best_for: People who want one app on their computer and TV to browse films and series, play them from add-ons they choose, and keep their library in sync.

points.title: Content comes from add-ons
points.text: Stremio provides no content itself. What you can find depends on the add-ons you install from its catalog.

points.title: Guest mode skips the sign-up
points.text: You can use it as a guest with no personal data, but then your library does not sync across devices.

points.title: Free, with supporter plans
points.text: The app is free and community funded. Paid Supporter plans give access to experimental features; the home page does not list their prices.

points.title: Windows listing tracks the 4.4 line
points.text: The Windows entries here are the older Stremio 4.4 series, a 32-bit per-user installer for Windows 10 or later, with 11 versions kept. Stremio's own download page now offers Stremio 5 for x64 and ARM64 Windows.

points.title: Mac is on Stremio 5
points.text: The Mac release here is 5.1.26, with separate Intel and Apple Silicon disk images. Stremio still offers 4.4 for macOS High Sierra and later, and 4.4.106 for El Capitan and Sierra.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is verified
points.text: Flathub marks the Flatpak as verified, published by Stremio, for x64 and ARM64, at about 54 MB. Stremio's site also offers a 4.4 .deb for Debian and Ubuntu. macOS and Linux list only the current release here.

points.title: Phones and TVs too
points.text: There are apps for Android, Android TV and LG TVs. iPhone and iPad users get Stremio Web, which does less than the apps.
